nodes.summary: For an instance $(n, E)$, its graph is the simple graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E$.
nodes.title: Graph of a HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a well-formed instance $(n, E)$ with $n \ge 3$ whose graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.
nodes.title: HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is feasible when $n \ge 3$ and its graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, that is, a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once.
nodes.title: Feasible HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instances

nodes.summary: An instance of HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) is a pair $(n, E)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, and a finite list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the edges.
nodes.title: Instances of HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED)

nodes.summary: The decision problem HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: If the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier accepts the bit strings $x$ and $y$, then $|y| = mw$, where $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$ and $w$ is the least natural number with $m \le 2^w$, and moreover $|y| \le |x|$.
nodes.title: Size of an accepted Hamiltonian-cycle certificate

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a bit string and $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$, suppose $|x| = m^2$, and let $G$ be a simple graph on the vertices $0, \dots, m - 1$ in which $i$ and $j$ are adjacent exactly when entry $im + j$ of $x$ (counting from $0$) is true. If $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle, then there is a bit string $y$ of length $mw$, where $w$ is the least natural number with $m \le 2^w$, such that the Hamiltonian-cycle…
nodes.title: Completeness of the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be bit strings, $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$, and $w$ the least natural number with $m \le 2^w$. For each $i$ let $d_i$ be the number whose binary digits, least significant first, are the bits of $y$ at positions $iw, \dots, iw + w - 1$ (counting from $0$; positions past the end of $y$ are omitted). The Hamiltonian-cycle verifier accepts $x$ and $y$ if and only if $|x| = m^2$, $m \ge 3$,…
nodes.title: Acceptance condition of the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, with $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$, some bit string $y$ makes the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier accept $x$ and $y$ if and only if $|x| = m^2$, $m \ge 3$, and there is a simple graph $G$ on the vertices $0, \dots, m - 1$ in which $i$ and $j$ are adjacent exactly when entry $im + j$ of $x$ (counting from $0$) is true, and $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle.
nodes.title: Certificates exist exactly for Hamiltonian graphs

nodes.summary: If the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier accepts the bit strings $x$ and $y$, then, with $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$, we have $|x| = m^2$ and $m \ge 3$, and there is a simple graph $G$ on the vertices $0, \dots, m - 1$ in which $i$ and $j$ are adjacent exactly when entry $im + j$ of $x$ (counting from $0$) is true, and $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle.
nodes.title: Soundness of the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier

nodes.summary: There is a constant $c > 0$ such that for all bit strings $x$ and $y$ that the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier accepts, its step count on $x$ and $y$ is at most $c\,(|x| + 1)^2$.
nodes.title: Step bound for accepted Hamiltonian-cycle certificates

nodes.summary: There is a constant $c > 0$ such that for all bit strings $x$ and $y$, the step count of the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier on $x$ and $y$ is at most $c\,(|x| + |y| + 1)^2$.
nodes.title: Quadratic step bound for the Hamiltonian-cycle verifier

nodes.summary: Given bit strings $x$ and $y$, let $m = \lfloor \sqrt{|x|} \rfloor$ and let $w$ be the least natural number with $m \le 2^w$. The verifier reads $x$ as the adjacency matrix of a graph on the vertices $0, \dots, m - 1$, stored row by row, and $y$ as $m$ words of $w$ bits, the $i$-th word giving a number $v_i$ in binary, least significant bit first. nodes.title: Hamiltonian-cycle verifier

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, E)$ is well formed when $0 < n$, the list $E$ has no repeated entries, and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and its reversal $(v, u)$ does not belong to $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed HAMILTONIAN CYCLE (UNDIRECTED) instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
